decision: Bounded v1: instant client-side search over curated, evidence-graded layers plus a linked crate directory; deeper indexing later.
First new-repo cohort covers all six repositories created after the 44.

v1 sources are curated layers only: this repo's practices, readiness gates, techniques, failure modes, lessons, checklist, verdicts and stack verdicts; fh's five catalogs restricted to rows citing public Dicklesworthstone code; rigor-atlas prescriptions, kinds, crate profiles and techniques (pointer-only); a crate directory built from public GitHub. fh and rigor-atlas are read as dated, hashed snapshots, never as runtime services.
rationale: fh measured rank-1 relevance 0/37 on build-intent queries at 8-12 s per query over 1.9M raw documents (intake-IntakeFH2); curated rows carry intent and evidence

decision: Pointer-only for Jeffrey's material: results carry our own words plus links to repo/path:line at a pinned commit; no verbatim code or evidence quotes from rider-licensed repos are republished, no builds of his code are hosted.
rationale: the rider counts making the software or derivatives available to Restricted Parties as prohibited, and a public page is available to everyone; linking avoids the question (intake-IntakeRigor2, intake-IntakeEco2)
reversibility: reversible (quotes can be added later if the maintainer decides UNK-006)

decision: Search engine: a small in-house client-side index (no service). frankensearch is not used in v1.
rationale: frankensearch has no WASM or browser path (memmap2, rayon, libc; 621 MB models) and hosting a build publicly conflicts with its rider (intake-IntakeEco2)

decision: License shown for a crate comes from its repository's root LICENSE file at the pinned commit, never from Cargo.toml metadata or crates.io.
rationale: 333 crates say MIT in metadata while their repos ship the rider LICENSE; one crates.io tarball ships no LICENSE (intake-IntakeEco2)

decision: Every indexed item gets a namespaced ID (fr:RP-001, fr:gate-7, fh:rigor-L3, ra:tech-123, crate:<repo>/<crate>) because source ID families collide (A1, G1 each mean two or three things).
Keep the site open to every crawler, but disallow known AI-lab crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Google-Extended, CCBot) from the quote-bearing index shard only, via robots.txt.
rationale: quotes of rider-licensed code on a public page are readable by the barred labs' crawlers; our own content stays open to everyone

decision: Short verbatim quotes of Jeffrey's code or docs are allowed: a few lines, cited repo/path:line at a pinned commit, with the source repository's license, the MIT notice, and a plain rider flag where it applies. No hosted builds of his code.

Search engine shape: candidate A, a build-time inverted index with prefix support and BM25-style scoring, queried on the main thread; core shard 102.0 KB brotli, full index 444.4 KB, quotes shard 124.6 KB stored and never indexed.
alternatives: B: A in a Web Worker (slower to type; phone load p95 1,560 ms fails the 1,000 ms budget)
C: vendored MiniSearch (6.7x slower per query; 7.7x p50 to 20x p95 slower to hydrate)
evidence: probe commit a55f8fd, .atlas-arc/artifacts/perf/20260925T005518Z-ebac079/; optimisation run .atlas-arc/artifacts/perf/20260925T175730Z-4b31427/ (engine A + L1 bounded top-k + L2 dense accumulators + L3a in-place result rows: phone keystroke p95 8.0 ms in 2 invocations vs incumbent 16.4/15.8 ms, desktop 1.8 ms; golden-diff 0 changed rows incl. the 88-query golden set)
open: Phone keystroke p95 18.0 ms (quiet passes) misses the 16 ms budget. Hotspots: frame work after layout (p95 13.1 ms), input queueing (6.8 ms; floor 5.1 ms), forced layout of the results list (6.1 ms), engine search (p95 8.9 ms; selectTopK is about 60% of it). The host was shared (load 37 to 67), so the phone numbers need a quiet re-run before tuning.

decision: Crawler policy is open: the site, including the quotes shard, carries no crawler-specific rule. search/crawler-policy is set to `open`, so quotes flow under DEC-009's citation, license and rider-flag rules.
alternatives: DEC-008: disallow AI-lab crawlers from the quotes shard only
rationale: maintainer's choice when asked; robots.txt is a request, not enforcement, and every quote already carries its license and rider flag
